fields.aka: Bhakti Vedānta Vāmana, Santoṣa (childhood name), Sajjana-sevaka Brahmacārī, Bhaktivedānta Vāmana Mahārāja
fields.appearance: Pauṣa Kṛṣṇa Navamī (Gauḍīya calendar); 23 December 1921 (another text: 1916), at Piljaṅgā (Khulna)
fields.place: Born at Piljaṅgā, Khulna district (another text: Jessore), East Bengal; Māyāpura (Bhaktivinoda Institute); Devānanda Gauḍīya Maṭha, Navadvīpa (Śrī Gauḍīya Vedānta Samiti); centres at Purī, Tura, Dhubri, Guwahati, Silchar
fields.guru: Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja (dīkṣā, given through the prison bars; sannyāsa on Gaura Pūrṇimā 1952); harināma from Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī in 1936; sacred thread from Bhakti Vicāra Yāyāvara Mahārāja
fields.disciples: Śrīpāda Mādhava Mahārāja; śikṣā-guru of Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja
fields.works: Did all the work of the Śrī Gauḍīya Patrikā (from 1948); republished the Gītā with Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa's commentary, Jaiva-dharma, Prema-pradīpa, Prabandhāvalī, Śaraṇāgati, Navadvīpa-bhāva-taraṅga and other books
fields.notes: Father: Satiścandra Ghoṣa (Sarveśvara Dāsādhikārī after dīkṣā from Keśava Mahārāja); mother: Bhagavatī Devī, disciple of Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī; paternal uncle: Bhakti Kuśala Nṛsiṁha Mahārāja. In the maṭha from boyhood (1931) under Vinodabihārī Brahmacārī. Lifelong naiṣṭhika brahmacārī. President and ācārya of the Gauḍīya Vedānta Samiti from 1968. Famous for quoting scripture from memory ('a dictionary of ślokas').

fields.aka: Gaura Nārāyaṇa, Bhaktabandhava, Nārāyaṇa Tivārī (birth name), Bholānātha, Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Mahārāja
fields.appearance: Māgha Amāvasyā, Maunī Amāvasyā (Gauḍīya calendar); 7 February 1921 (another text: 19 February), at Tivārīpura (Buxar)
fields.place: Born at Tivārīpura (Buxar district, Bihar); Sahibganj and Rājmahal (police service); Navadvīpa (dīkṣā 1947); in charge of the Keśavajī Gauḍīya Maṭha, Mathurā, from 1954; Bengal; from 1996 preaching all over the world
fields.guru: Śrīla Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja (harināma and dīkṣā on Gaura Pūrṇimā 1947; sannyāsa on Gaura Pūrṇimā 1952)
fields.works: Hindi translations of Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura's books (Jaiva-dharma, Caitanya-śikṣāmṛta, Bhakti-tattva-viveka, Vaiṣṇava-siddhānta-mālā), Upadeśāmṛta, Śikṣāṣṭaka, Manaḥ-śikṣā, Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu-bindu, Gauḍīya Kaṇṭhahāra, the Gītā with Viśvanātha Cakravartī's commentary; many books translated into English and other languages; editor of Śrī Bhāgavata Patrikā
fields.notes: Father: Paṇḍita Baleśvaranātha Tivārī; mother: Lakṣmī Devī; Trivedī brāhmaṇa family. Joined through Narottamānanda Brahmacārī; met his guru in Navadvīpa in February 1947. Vice-president of the Gauḍīya Vedānta Samiti; performed the sannyāsa fire sacrifice (1959) and the samādhi rites (1977) of A.C. Bhaktivedānta Svāmī, and the samādhi of Keśava Mahārāja (1968). Organised the yearly Kārtika Vraja-maṇḍala parikramā. Founding member of the WVA.

fields.name: Śrīla Gour Govinda Svāmī Mahārāja
fields.aka: Gour Govinda Mahārāja, Gaura Govinda Svāmī, Gour Govinda Gosvāmī Mahārāja, Braja-bandhu Giri (birth name)
fields.appearance: Bhādra Śukla Dvitīyā (Gauḍīya calendar); 2 September 1929, at Jagannātha-pura near Purī (Orissa)
fields.disappearance: Phālguna Kṛṣṇa Pañcamī (Gauḍīya calendar); 9 February 1996, Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī's appearance day
fields.place: Born at Jagannātha-pura, near Jagannātha Purī (Orissa); grew up at Gadāi-giri; Vṛndāvana (sannyāsa 1975); Bhubaneswar (Kṛṣṇa-Balarāma temple, 1991)
fields.guru: Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Prabhupāda (initiation and sannyāsa, Vṛndāvana 1975)
fields.works: Translations of Bhaktivedānta Svāmī's books into Oriyā; books from his talks: Simplicity and Faith, How to Find a Sādhu, The Embankment of Separation
fields.notes: Of the Giri family of Gadāi-giri, kīrtana singers of Orissa since Śyāmānanda's time; worshipped the family Deity Gopāla Jīu from six. Married Śrīmatī Vasantī Devī; B.A. and B.Ed. (Utkal University); schoolteacher. Left home on 8 April 1974. Built the Śrī Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Balarāma temple at Bhubaneswar, whose foundation stone Bhaktivedānta Svāmī laid in 1977. Śikṣā-guru of Rādhānātha dāsa.

fields.name: Śrīla Bhakti Sundara Govinda Dev-Gosvāmī Mahārāja
fields.aka: Sundar Govinda Dev Goswami Mahārāj, Bhakti Sundar Govinda Dev-Gosvāmī Mahārāj, Śrīla Govinda Mahārāja, Vidyā-rañjana
fields.disappearance: 27 March 2010; samādhi at the Śrī Caitanya Sārasvata Maṭha, Navadvīpa
fields.place: Born at Bāmunpāḍā, Burdwan district (West Bengal); Śrī Caitanya Sārasvata Maṭha, Navadvīpa (samādhi mandir); Calcutta; centres on six continents
fields.guru: Śrīla Bhakti Rakṣaka Śrīdhara Deva Gosvāmī Mahārāja (sannyāsa 1985)
fields.works: Editor of Śrī Gauḍīya Darśana; poems and articles in Sanskrit and Bengali; Religion of the Heart, Dignity of the Divine Servitor, Golden Reflections, Divine Guidance; over 350 publications in twenty languages
fields.notes: Of a brāhmaṇa family of followers of Nityānanda; served the family Deities Rādhā-Gopīnātha installed by Vīracandra Prabhu. Met Śrīdhara Mahārāja at seventeen and lived with him forty-two years as servant, doctor and confidant. Started the maṭha's Navadvīpa parikramā (1948); first distributor of Back to Godhead for A.C. Bhaktivedānta Svāmī. President-sevaite-ācārya of the Śrī Caitanya Sārasvata Maṭha from 1986; toured the world 24 times.

fields.aka: Bhakti Vallabha Tīrtha, Ballabh Thirta Gosvāmī, Bhakti Ballabh Tīrtha Gosvāmī Mahārāja, B.B. Tīrtha Mahārāja
fields.appearance: Caitra Śukla Navamī, Rāma Navamī (Gauḍīya calendar); 24 April 1924, at Amlapatti, Goalpara (Assam)
fields.place: Born at Amlapatti, Goalpara (Assam); Calcutta University; Śrī Caitanya Gauḍīya Maṭha; world tours from 1997
fields.guru: Śrīla Bhakti Dayita Mādhava Gosvāmī Mahārāja (sannyāsa 1961); śikṣā from Bhakti Pramoda Purī Gosvāmī Mahārāja
fields.works: Śuddha Bhakti, Sages of Ancient India, A Taste of Transcendence, Śrī Caitanya: His Life and Associates, Dāśāvatāra, Kārtika Handbook
fields.notes: M.A. in philosophy (Calcutta University); joined the Śrī Caitanya Gauḍīya Maṭha in 1947 and was its secretary. President-ācārya of the Śrī Caitanya Gauḍīya Maṭha from 1979, by his guru's nomination; founder-ācārya of GOKUL (1997); vice-president of the WVA. Addressed the United Nations in New York (1997).

fields.aka: Gaura Govindānanda Bhāgavata, Gauragovinda, Bhāgavata Svāmī
fields.place: Born in Jessore district (Bangladesh); Kāśī (Vedānta under Paramānanda Tīrtha, c. 1903); Mathurā (Kṛṣṇagaṅgā, 1905-06); Govardhana (a year of silence); seven years in a cave at Kāmyavana; preached in Sylhet, Tripura, Silchar, Dhaka and Mymensingh
fields.guru: Kṛpā from a Vaiṣṇava bābājī who blessed him at his death; Devagiri Muni of Mathurā (śikṣā)
fields.works: Kṛpā-kusumāñjali (1935), Sādhana-kusumāñjali (1936), Śrī Guru-vaiṣṇava-bhakti-kusumāñjali (1940), Śrī Līlā-tattva-kusumāñjali (1941)
fields.notes: Born into a high caste brāhmaṇa family in Jessore district, Bangladesh; parents died when he was young. Raised by his maternal grandfather Sanyal Mahāśaya. Left home at 13-14 to travel with a brahmacārī. Became a scholar of all śāstras without formal study, by the blessing of a saint; associated with Bholānanda Giri, Kṛṣṇaprasāda dāsa Bābājī (Gudhi Bābā), Siddha Jagadīśa Bābā and Rāmadāsa Kāṭhiyā Bābā.
